title: Half Adder Simulator
description: A half adder is a logic circuit that adds two 1-bit numbers. Given two bits A and B, simulate a half adder by outputting the Sum and Carry bits.
inputFormat: Two space-separated integers A and B, where each is either 0 or 1.
outputFormat: Two space-separated integers representing Sum and Carry.
note: Sum = A XOR B, Carry = A AND B.

title: Full Adder Simulator
description: A full adder adds three 1-bit numbers (A, B, and Cin). Given A, B, and Cin, simulate a full adder by outputting the Sum and Carry (Cout) bits.
inputFormat: Three space-separated integers A, B, and Cin, where each is either 0 or 1.
outputFormat: Two space-separated integers representing Sum and Cout.
note: Sum = A XOR B XOR Cin. Cout = (A AND B) OR (Cin AND (A XOR B)).

title: Half Subtractor Simulator
description: A half subtractor is a logic circuit that subtracts two 1-bit numbers. Given two bits A and B (A - B), simulate a half subtractor by outputting the Difference and Borrow bits.
inputFormat: Two space-separated integers A and B, where each is either 0 or 1.
outputFormat: Two space-separated integers representing Difference and Borrow.
note: Difference = A XOR B, Borrow = (NOT A) AND B.

title: Full Subtractor Simulator
description: A full subtractor subtracts a subtrahend and a borrow-in bit from a minuend (A - B - Bin). Given A, B, and Bin, output the Difference and Borrow-out (Bout) bits.
inputFormat: Three space-separated integers A, B, and Bin, where each is either 0 or 1.
outputFormat: Two space-separated integers representing Difference and Bout.
note: Difference = A XOR B XOR Bin. Bout = ((NOT A) AND B) OR (((NOT A) XOR B) AND Bin).

title: Binary to Gray Code Converter
description: Given a binary string of length N, convert it to its corresponding Gray code.
inputFormat: A single string representing a binary number.
outputFormat: A single string representing the Gray code.
note: The MSB of Gray code is same as binary. The subsequent bits are G[i] = B[i] XOR B[i-1].

title: Gray to Binary Code Converter
description: Given a Gray code string of length N, convert it back to its corresponding binary string.
inputFormat: A single string representing a Gray code.
outputFormat: A single string representing the Binary number.
note: The MSB of binary is same as Gray. B[i] = B[i-1] XOR G[i].

title: Multiply Two 16-bit Numbers
description: Write a program to multiply two 16-bit unsigned integers. Output the 32-bit product.
inputFormat: Two space-separated integers A and B.
outputFormat: A single integer representing the product.
note: Simulates an ALP multiplier that stores a 32-bit result.

title: Sum of First N Integers
description: Write a program to find the sum of the first N natural numbers. (Simulates an assembly loop counting from 1 to N).
inputFormat: A single integer N.
outputFormat: A single integer representing the sum.
note: You can use formula N*(N+1)/2 or a loop.

title: Factorial of a Number
description: Write a program to find the factorial of a number N. Output 1 if N=0.
inputFormat: A single integer N (0 <= N <= 12).
outputFormat: A single integer representing N!.
note: Simulates a looping multiplication sequence in ALP.

title: Add Array of 16-bit Numbers
description: Given an array of N 16-bit unsigned integers, compute their sum and output the 32-bit result. This simulates accumulating memory values in a 32-bit register.
inputFormat: The first line contains N. The second line contains N space-separated integers.
outputFormat: A single integer representing the sum.
note: Sum can exceed 16-bit limit.

title: Count Ones in a Binary Number
description: Given a 32-bit unsigned integer, write a program to count the number of ones (1s) in its binary representation.
inputFormat: A single integer N.
outputFormat: A single integer representing the count of ones.
note: Also known as Hamming weight.

title: Count Zeros in a Binary Number
description: Given a 32-bit unsigned integer, write a program to count the number of zeros (0s) in its 32-bit binary representation.
inputFormat: A single unsigned integer N (0 <= N <= 2^32 - 1).
outputFormat: A single integer representing the count of zeros.
note: Ensure you consider the 32-bit format. For N=0, the answer is 32.

title: Stepper Motor Sequence (Clockwise)
description: Simulate the full-step sequence of a stepper motor in clockwise direction. The 4 states are 1000, 0100, 0010, 0001 repeating. Given an initial state (as a 4-bit string) and a number of steps N, output the state reached after N steps.
inputFormat: A 4-bit string representing the initial state, followed by an integer N.
outputFormat: A 4-bit string representing the final state.

title: Stepper Motor Sequence (Anti-Clockwise)
description: Simulate the full-step sequence of a stepper motor in anti-clockwise direction. The 4 states are 1000, 0001, 0010, 0100 repeating. Given an initial state and N steps, output the final state.
inputFormat: A 4-bit string representing the initial state, followed by an integer N.
outputFormat: A 4-bit string representing the final state.

title: 7-Segment Display Encoder
description: In embedded systems, hex digits are displayed using 7-segment displays. Write a program to convert a hex character (0-9, A-F) to its 8-bit binary common-cathode representation. Segments are a,b,c,d,e,f,g,dp. Assume dp is always 0, and mapping is MSB to LSB: dp g f e d c b a. For example, '0' lights up a,b,c,d,e,f -> 00111111.
inputFormat: A single uppercase character representing the hex digit.
outputFormat: An 8-bit binary string.
note: Example for '1': lights b,c -> 00000110. '8' lights all except dp -> 01111111.

title: UART Message Simulator
description: Simulate UART transmission for a given string. For each character, print a 10-bit frame: 1 Start bit (0), 8 Data bits (binary representation of ASCII, LSB first), and 1 Stop bit (1). Output frames space-separated.
inputFormat: A single string (without spaces).
outputFormat: A space-separated sequence of 10-bit binary strings.
note: For character 'A' (ASCII 65 = 01000001), LSB first is 10000010. Frame = 0 10000010 1 = 0100000101.

title: DC Motor PWM Duty Cycle
description: Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) controls DC motor speed. Given the total time period T and a duty cycle percentage D, calculate the ON time and OFF time.
inputFormat: Two space-separated integers T and D.
outputFormat: Two space-separated integers representing ON time and OFF time (rounded down if necessary).
note: ON = (T * D) / 100. OFF = T - ON.

title: Button Press Edge Detector
description: A Raspberry Pi reads button states every 10ms. Given a sequence of button states (0 for released, 1 for pressed), count how many distinct button presses occurred. A press is a transition from 0 to 1.
inputFormat: The first line contains N (number of readings). The second line contains N space-separated states (0 or 1).
outputFormat: A single integer representing the number of presses.
note: Start by assuming the previous state was 0.

title: LED Toggle Pattern
description: An LED is interfaced to a Raspberry Pi and toggled every cycle. Given an initial state (0 or 1) and N cycles, output the sequence of states.
inputFormat: Two space-separated integers: initial state and N.
outputFormat: A sequence of N space-separated integers representing the state in each cycle.
note: Example: If initial=0 and N=4, output is 0 1 0 1.

title: Boolean Expression Evaluator
description: In the laboratory, you realized expressions using logic gates. Evaluate Y = (A AND B) OR (C AND D) for given binary inputs A, B, C, D.
inputFormat: Four space-separated integers A, B, C, D (0 or 1).
outputFormat: A single integer representing the output Y (0 or 1).
note: Simple logical operations.

title: Even Parity Generator
description: In communication interfaces like UART, a parity bit is often added. Given an 8-bit binary string, append an EVEN parity bit at the end. Even parity means the total number of 1s in the 9-bit string should be even.
inputFormat: An 8-bit binary string.
outputFormat: A 9-bit binary string.
note: If the 8-bit string has an odd number of 1s, append '1', else append '0'.

title: Odd Parity Generator
description: Given an 8-bit binary string, append an ODD parity bit at the end. Odd parity means the total number of 1s in the 9-bit string should be odd.
inputFormat: An 8-bit binary string.
outputFormat: A 9-bit binary string.
note: If the 8-bit string has an even number of 1s, append '1', else append '0'.

title: Arithmetic Logic Unit Simulator
description: Simulate a basic ALU that takes two integers A and B, and a 2-bit opcode as a string. Operations: 00 -> ADD, 01 -> SUBTRACT (A-B), 10 -> BITWISE AND, 11 -> BITWISE OR. Output the result.
inputFormat: Two integers A and B, followed by a 2-bit string opcode.
outputFormat: A single integer representing the result.
note: Be mindful of negative results for SUBTRACT.

title: Bitwise Set/Clear/Toggle
description: In embedded programming, manipulating individual bits is critical. Given an integer N, a bit position P (0 is LSB), and an operation code (1: Set, 2: Clear, 3: Toggle). Output the modified integer.
inputFormat: Three space-separated integers N, P, and OP.
outputFormat: A single integer representing the new value.
note: Set turns the bit to 1, Clear to 0, Toggle flips it.

title: Loop Delay Calculator
description: An embedded processor runs a simple delay loop. If one iteration of the loop takes exactly K milliseconds, calculate the number of iterations required to achieve a total delay of exactly D milliseconds. Assume D is a multiple of K.
inputFormat: Two space-separated integers D and K.
outputFormat: A single integer representing the number of iterations.
note: Iterations = D / K.
